codeReview.summary: The fix successfully addresses all three aspects of the original blocking bug: (1) the dead-code ternary with identical branches has been replaced with a clean hasOverride conditional that either uses deriveFrameworkFromOverride or falls back to detectTestFramework; (2) when an override is provided, language and testCommand are now correctly derived from the override name via deriveFrameworkFromOverride rather than taken from the auto-detected framework; (3) PromptBuildContext.testFramework is now optional (testFramework?: string) in types.ts. The new deriveFrameworkFromOverride function maps 5 well-known frameworks (pytest, unittest, vitest, jest, mocha) with sensible defaults, and includes heuristic fallback for unknown names and whitespace trimming. 10 new tests comprehensively cover the fix. The remaining non-blocking issues from the prior review (unused imports, extractGoal type assertions) were not addressed by this fix feature, which is appropriate since they were not part of the fix scope.

issues.description: Pre-existing: unused type imports ExecuteWorkstream and PlanItem remain. These were flagged in the prior review as non-blocking and are not part of this fix's scope, but should be cleaned up eventually.
Pre-existing: extractGoal uses overly broad type assertions (carry_forward cast and purpose cast). These were flagged in the prior review as non-blocking and are not part of this fix's scope.

deriveFrameworkFromOverride heuristic for detecting 'python-like' frameworks via name.includes('py') could produce false positives for frameworks like 'pylint' or 'pyroscope' that aren't test frameworks. However, this is a minor concern since the function is only called when the user explicitly provides a testFramework override — if they provide 'pylint', they are already providing a non-test-framework name. The catch-all fallback is reasonable for this use case.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The deriveFrameworkFromOverride function uses a simple if-else chain for framework mapping rather than a lookup Map/object. Both patterns exist in the codebase (detectTestFramework uses if-else, detectTestFramework in execute may use maps). There's no documented convention for when to use which pattern.

summary: The fix adequately addresses ALL aspects of the original blocking failure. The three original problems were: (1) Dead code branch — both ternary branches called detectTestFramework. FIXED: Now uses `hasOverride ? deriveFrameworkFromOverride(...) : detectTestFramework(...)` with distinct branches. (2) Override used detected framework's language/testCommand — if user provided 'vitest' on a jest project, they'd get {name:'vitest', language:'typescript', testCommand:'npx jest'} which is wrong. FIXED: deriveFrameworkFromOverride correctly maps framework names to their own language/testCommand (e.g., vitest→typescript/npx vitest run, pytest→python/pytest). (3) PromptBuildContext.testFramework was required instead of optional. FIXED: Changed to `testFramework?: string` in types.ts. 10 new tests cover deriveFrameworkFromOverride (8 tests) and buildIntegrationTestPrompt override behavior (2 tests), plus the existing override test was enhanced to verify derived language and testCommand. All 43 prompt-builder tests pass. The pre-existing non-blocking issues (unused imports, extractGoal type assertions) remain but are appropriately out of scope for this fix.
